newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Plutonic says stronger now than a year ago.
newsitem.headline: Plutonic says stronger now than a year ago.

text.p: Gold miner Plutonic Resources Ltd said on Tuesday it ended 1996 stronger than at the start of the year.
"All in all, we leave the year more strongly than we began," Plutonic's chairman told an annual shareholders' meeting.
He said longer-term the recently discovered Centenary deposit seems likely to have the capacity to match the company's main Plutonic mine in contributing to results in 1999.
The two deposits hold the potential to produce significant cash surpluses, even at relatively subdued gold prices, the chairman said.
Plutonic was "absolutely committed" to development of underground mining at both deposits as well as on exploration, he said.
A focus on mine development will not be at the expense of growth via exploration and acquisitions, he said.
Plutonic earlier this year reported a 1996 net profit of A$40.70 million versus A$40.12 million in 1995.
Plutonic is about 30 percent owned by Malaysia Mining Corp Bhd
